introduction.p: In this activity, we will consider some simple examples that will guide us in finding a more general approach.

solution.p: The equations tell us the value of both variables so there is only one solution (x,y) = (2,-1).

Notice that we can rewrite the first equation as x=-1-3y and substitute this into the second equation to obtain
2(-1-3y)+y = -2 -5y = 3.
This tells us that y=-1 and x=-1-3y = 2. The linear system therefore has one solution (x,y) = (2,-1).

statement.p: Describe the solution space to the linear equation 0x = 0.

solution.p: No matter the value of x, we have 0x = 0. Therefore, the solution space to the equation 0x=0 is all real numbers x. In other words, this equation does not place a restriction on the value of x.

answer.p: Any real number is a solution.

statement.p: Describe the solution space to the linear equation 0x = 5.

solution.p: By contrast, the equation 0x=5 has no solutions since no value of x, when multiplied by 0, can produce 5.
